lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Where are all the beautiful men and women, Hermes? Give me the tour. I'm new here.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I'm on the clock, Menippus. Just look over there to the right. That's Hyacinthus, and Narcissus, Nireus, Achilles, Tyro, Helen, Leda—basically the entire classic beauty section.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All I see are bones. Bare skulls. Mostly identical.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Well, those are the bones the poets rave about. The ones you seem so unimpressed by.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Still, point out Helen for me. I couldn't possibly tell them apart.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: [taps a skull] This skull right here is Helen.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [pause] And *this* is what a thousand ships from all over Greece were launched for? This is why so many Greeks and barbarians fell, and so many cities were wiped out?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You didn't see the woman when she was alive, Menippus. Even you would have quoted the poets: 'no shame to suffer long for such a woman.' It's like dried flowers. If you look at them after they've lost their pigment, obviously they look ugly. But when they're in bloom and have their color, they're stunning.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That's exactly what amazes me, Hermes. The Greeks went to all that trouble without realizing they were fighting over something so short-lived, that loses its petals so fast.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: [sighs] I don't have time to stand around philosophizing with you, Menippus. Pick a spot, wherever you like, and park yourself. I have to go fetch the next batch of dead.
